chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUlwān, from Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf, from al-Aṣbagh ibn Nubātah, who said:

A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, may I kiss while I am fasting?” He عليه السلام said to him: “Keep your fast chaste, for the beginning of fighting is the slap.”

So these two reports are to be understood as indicating a kind of karahah, because what is better is that a person should not expose himself to these things, in order to keep his fast above reproach and to avoid that with which he would not be safe from committing what is prohibited.

key_terms.اللِّطَامُ: the slap; the initial act that begins escalation

ai.seo_question: Is kissing while fasting considered forbidden or merely disliked in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling on kissing while fasting and indicates that it is regarded with karahah rather than absolute prohibition. The closing explanation clarifies that avoiding such acts is better, so that one preserves the dignity of the fast and stays away from what may lead to the prohibited.
